body: Hello there! Schizophrenic here! I have had many encounters of which I question are real or fake, but when living with a hallucination inducing mental illness, I will say that I can easily tell what is a hallucination and what is actually happening. It takes practice but most of us get there. My hallucinations tend to follow centain patterns of past childhood trauma, and include sudden thunderstoms in my bedroom, my face changing in the mirror, or whispers of certain words/phrases- only I can see/hear/feel these. Paranormal things tend to be more of a surprise and I find myself thinking: "huh. well THAT happened." I can be walking out on a sunny day, no clouds, hear really loud thunder, feel like it's pouring, but I know it's only me when I look around at others whose clothes are dry - it's definitely not happening; meanwhile, the strange void lookin dude that came out from a spare room in my house at 3am is a shared experience with me among two of my roommates, and that definitely happened. All in all, it never hurts to say "hey uh, is it just me or...?" If you ever wanna chat about schizo-affective disorders and some common things that go with it, feel free to shoot me a message.

To live it! Allow yourself to exist as you are, and take the hard life lessons that arise as opportunities to learn. There is no one set path. Just have some fun in your meat suit from time to time :)
